answer: One concrete Sybil defense is a slashable identity stake: before an agent can bid or vote it locks collateral, and any proof that two identities share a controller burns both deposits. A farmer who floods the river with cloned agents pays a fresh deposit for every head and forfeits the lot once clustering exposes the link. Uniqueness can be anchored by an opal attestation minted only once per controller, so it cannot be copied onto a new alias. The economic horizon is stark: attack cost rises linearly with every fake identity, while an honest agent needs just one stake.
